title: Ensure VRRP authentication-key is set (VRRP)
description: VRRP authentication should be used where other security mechanisms are not in place. VRRP provides resilience for a routers interfaces, allowing another router to act as backup in the event of a partial or complete failure of the primary router and increasing the availability network resources as well as resilience to DoS attack. Passes when VRRP is not configured; otherwise requires an authentication-key on the VRRP groups. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 3.2.1 Ensure VRRP authentication-key is set

remediation.command:
! If you have configured VRRP on one or more interfaces you should configure authentication using the following commands from the hierarchy;
set interfaces `<interface name> unit <unit number> family inet address <ip address>` vrrp-group <group number> authentication-key <key>

title: Ensure authentication-type is set to MD5 (VRRP)
description: Any VRRP authentication should use MD5 HMAC. VRRP provides resilience for a routers interfaces, allowing another router to act as backup in the event of a partial or complete failure of the primary router and increasing the availability network resources as well as resilience to DoS attack. Passes when VRRP is not configured; otherwise requires 'authentication-type md5'. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 3.2.2 Ensure authentication-type is set to MD5

remediation.command:
! If you have configured VRRP on one or more interfaces you can configure authentication using MD5-HMAC with the following commands from the hierarchy;
set interfaces <interface name> unit <unit number> family inet address <ip address> vrrp-group <group number> authentication-type md5

title: Ensure peer authentication is set to MD5 (BGP)
description: BGP Peers should be authenticated. Where it is deployed, BGP routing is vital for normal operation of an organization's network infrastructure. Correct route information is required for routers to correctly direct traffic through the network. Passes when BGP is not configured; otherwise requires an authentication-key at global, group or neighbor level. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.1.1 Ensure peer authentication is set to MD5

remediation.command:
! If you have deployed BGP in your network you should authenticate all neighbors. Authentication can be configured at the Global, Group or Neighbor level, with more specific settings overriding less specific. For eBGP a different MD5 password should be configured for each neighbor or peer. For iBGP neighbors the same key may be used globally or different keys may be used by group or neighbor as appropriate to your infrastructure. To configure BGP Authentication at the globally enter the following command at the hierarchy:
set protocols bgp authentication-key <md5 key> To configure BGP Authentication at the group level enter the following command at the hierarchy:
set protocols bgp group <group name> authentication-key <md5 key> Finally, to configure BGP Authentication at the neighbor level enter the following command at the hierarchy:
set protocols bgp group <group name> neighbor <neighbor IP> authentication-key <md5 key> Remember that more specific settings override less specific settings, so a key set at the neighbor level will be used even if keys are also set at the group and global levels.

title: Ensure IS-IS neighbor authentication is set to SHA1
description: IS-IS Neighbors should be authenticated with stronger SHA1 HMAC mechanism, where supported. Where it is deployed, IS-IS routing is vital for normal operation of an organization's network infrastructure. Correct route information is required for routers to correctly direct traffic through the network. Passes when IS-IS is not configured. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.2.2 Ensure IS-IS neighbor authentication is set to SHA1

remediation.command:
! If you have deployed IS-IS in your network you should consider configuring Hitless Key Rollover with SHA1 authentication for all neighbors at each IS-IS Level configured. First a key-chain must be configured. The same key-chain may be used for multiple levels or separate key-chains used for each level (or even for individual interfaces where required). From the hierarchy issue the following commands:
set security authentication-key-chains key-chain <name> key <key number> secret "<secret key>"
set security authentication-key-chains key-chain <name> key <key number> start-time "<yyyy-mm-dd.hh:mm:ss>"
set security authentication-key-chains key-chain <name> key <key number> algorithm hmac-sha-1
set security authentication-key-chains key-chain <name> key <key number> options isis-enhanced The start-time must be provided for all keys and provides the mechanism for controlled key rollover. Keys with a start time in the future can be configured across all of the devices in advance, when the time is reached all of the devices will hitlessly rollover to the new keys without disruption to IS-IS Adjacencies. title: Ensure OSPF authentication is set to MD5
description: OSPF Neighbors should be authenticated. Where it is deployed, OSPF routing is vital for normal operation of an organization's network infrastructure. Correct route information is required for routers to correctly direct traffic through the network. Passes when OSPF is not configured; otherwise requires MD5 authentication on OSPF interfaces. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.3.1 Ensure OSPF authentication is set to MD5

remediation.command:
! To configure MD5 based authentication, first configure the authentication type at the hierarchy (this step is not required on all versions of JUNOS):
set protocols ospf area <area number> authentication-type md5 The key must then be configured for any interfaces in the area
set protocols ospf area <area number> interface <interface number> authentication md5 <key number> <key> The parameter needs to be the same across all routers in the area and is there to provide a method for transitioning from old to new keys.

title: Ensure OSPF authentication is set to IPSEC SA with SHA
description: OSPF Neighbors should be strongly authenticated. Where it is deployed, OSPF routing is vital for normal operation of an organization's network infrastructure. Correct route information is required for routers to correctly direct traffic through the network. Passes when OSPF is not configured. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.3.2 Ensure OSPF authentication is set to IPSEC SA with SHA

remediation.command:
! To setup IPSEC SA based authentication, first configure a Security Association at the hierarchy; edit security-association <SA name> set description <description> set mode transport set manual direction bidirectional protocol ah set manual direction bidirectional algorithm hmac-sha1-96 set manual direction bidirectional authentication key <key> The SA must be bi-directional and must be configured with the same parameters on all neighbors reachable on the intended interface. Note that only Authenticated Header is configured in this example which provides mutual authentication but does not encrypt OSPF protocol messages in transit. Next configure IPSEC SA based authentication for one or more interfaces which OSPF will be run over from the hierarchy;
set protocols ospf area <area number> interface <interface number> ipsec-sa <SA name>

set protocols rip authentication-type md5
set protocols rip authentication-key <key>

title: Ensure BFD Authentication is Set
description: BFD Peers should be authenticated. Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) is a Forwarding Plane feature which allows more rapid detection of a failed neighbor then can be achieved through a routing protocols' normal detection mechanisms, providing faster reconvergence. Passes when BFD is not configured. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.6.1 Ensure BFD Authentication is Set

remediation.command:
! If you have deployed BFD, authentication can be configured by issuing the following commands. First set the authentication algorithm and keychain from the appropriate [.* bfd-liveness-detection] hierarchy, in this example we are configuring BFD Authentication for OSPF Neighbors on Interface Ge-0/0/0.0:
set protocols ospf interface ge-0/0/0.0 bfd-liveness-detection authentication algorithm <algorithm>
set protocols ospf interface ge-0/0/0.0 bfd-liveness-detection authentication key-chain <key-chain> Where: - <algorithm> is either keyed-md5, keyed-sha-1, meticulous-keyed-md5 or meticulous-keyed-sha-1, which is preferred but is not compatible with NSR and other failover options. - <key-chain> is the name of a configured key-chain (see below). If a Key Chain is not already defined, you should create one by issuing the following command at the hierarchy:
! ... see the benchmark for the full procedure

title: Ensure BFD Authentication is Not Set to Loose-Check
description: BFD Peers should be authenticated. Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) is a Forwarding Plane feature which allows more rapid detection of a failed neighbor then can be achieved through a routing protocols' normal detection mechanisms, providing faster reconvergence. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.6.2 Ensure BFD Authentication is Not Set to Loose-Check

remediation.command:
! If you have deployed BFD with Loose Authentication Checking, it can be disabled by issuing the appropriate [.* bfd-liveness-detection] hierarchy, in this example we are configuring BFD Authentication for BGP:
delete protocols bgp bfd-liveness-detection authentication loose-check BFD may be configured at a wide variety of configuration hierarchies, for different Protocols, Routing Instances or even for Static Routes. The bfd-liveness-detection hierarchy is the same at each level it is used, so the Remediation Process is the same and should be applied at each hierarchy indicated in the Audit Procedure.

title: Ensure authentication is set to MD5 (LDP)
description: LDP peers should be authenticated. Where it is deployed, LDP is vital for normal operation of an MPLS network. LDP is used to determine Label mapping and populate the routers Forwarding Information Base (FIB). Passes when no LDP session is configured. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.7.1 Ensure authentication is set to MD5

remediation.command:
! If you have deployed LDP in your network you should use MD5 authentication for all neighbors. To configure authentication for a session-group enter the following command from the hierarchy:
set protocols ldp session-group <Destination IP Address or IP/Mask> authentication-key <key>

title: Ensure authentication is set to AES-CMAC (LDP)
description: LDP peers should be strongly authenticated. Where it is deployed, LDP is vital for normal operation of an MPLS network. LDP is used to determine Label mapping and populate the routers Forwarding Information Base (FIB). Passes when no LDP session is configured. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.7.2 Ensure authentication is set to AES-CMAC

remediation.command:
! If you have deployed LDP in your network you should use strong authentication for all neighbors. Both AES-CMAC and SHA1-HMAC authentication require a keychain to be configured on the device under the hierarchy with at least one key which has a start time in the past.
set security authentication-key-chains key-chain <name> key <key number> start-time <YYYY-MM-DD.HH:MM>
set security authentication-key-chains key-chain <name> key <key number> secret <secret key> The chosen algorithm and keychain should then be configured for all session groups from the hierarchy:
set protocols ldp session-group <Destination IP Address or IP/Mask> authentication-algorithm aes-128-cmac-96
set protocols ldp session-group <Destination IP Address or IP/Mask> authentication-key-chain <name> or for SHA1 :
set protocols ldp session-group <Destination IP Address or IP/Mask> authentication-algorithm hmac-sha-1-96
set protocols ldp session-group <Destination IP Address or IP/Mask> authentication-key-chain <name>

title: Ensure authentication is set to MD5 (MSDP)
description: MSDP Peers should be authenticated. When deployed MSDP it provides PIM-SM with information for routing Multicast traffic and is critical to operation of Multicast services on the network. If no authentication is used, an attacker may inject false information into the PIM-SM distribution tree, ... Passes when MSDP is not configured. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.8.1 Ensure authentication is set to MD5

remediation.command:
! If you have deployed MSDP, authentication can be configured on a peer by peer basis, by issuing the following command from the hierarchy:
set protocols msdp peer <peer address> authentication-key <key>

title: Ensure authentication is set to MD5 (RSVP)
description: RSVP Peers should be authenticated. RSVP messages may be abused by an attacker to interfere with QoS and Traffic Engineering services, resulting in poor performance or Denial of Service, or seek to attack the target router directly using weaknesses in the RSVP implementation. Passes when RSVP is not configured. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.11.1 Ensure authentication is set to MD5

remediation.command:
! If you have configured RSVP you can add authentication by issuing the following command from the hierarchy:
set protocols rsvp interface <interface name> authentication-key <key>

title: Ensure Common SNMP Community Strings are NOT used
description: Do not use common / default community strings. SNMP can be used to read, and sometime write, sensitive information about your router and network environment. When using SNMP Versions 1 and 2C (SNMPv2c) a community string is used to identify and, to a limited degree, authenticate Management Stations. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1 Ensure Common SNMP Community Strings are NOT used

remediation.command:
! If you have deployed SNMPv1 or SNMPv2c on your router using one of these strings, rename the community using the following command under the hierarchy;
rename snmp community <old community> to community <new community>

title: Ensure “Default Restrict” is set in all client lists
description: Limit clients to access SNMP. Even when limited to read only access, SNMP can provide an attacker with a wealth of information about your router and network topology. To limit the potential for attacks against your routers SNMP service your client lists should be configured to deny any ... Passes when no client-list exists; otherwise requires 'default restrict'. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.4 Ensure “Default Restrict” is set in all client lists

title: Ensure SNMP Write Access is not set
description: Do not allow Read-Write SNMP access. SNMP can be used to read and write configuration information from a router using your Network Management Systems; however the inherently insecure design of the older SNMP V1, V2 and V2C standards, which do not use encryption to protect community strings, make ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.5 Ensure SNMP Write Access is not set

title: Ensure SHA1 is set for SNMPv3 authentication
description: Do not allow unauthenticated SNMPv3 access. SNMPv3 provides much improved security over previous versions by offering options for Authentication and Encryption of messages. Authentication in SNMPv3 is performed using Keyed-Hash Message Authentication Code or HMAC. Passes when no SNMPv3 user exists; fails on MD5/none authentication. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.7 Ensure SHA1 is set for SNMPv3 authentication

remediation.command:
! For each SNMPv3 user created on your router add privacy options by issuing the following command from the hierarchy;
set snmp v3 usm local-engine user <username> authentication-sha authentication-password <password>

title: Ensure interface restrictions are set for SNMP
description: SNMP should only be configured on required interfaces. By default the SNMP service will listen for incoming connections on all interfaces which have an IP Address configured, exposing SNMP to users on all networks through which the router is reachable. Passes when SNMP is not configured; otherwise requires 'set snmp interface'. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.8 Ensure interface restrictions are set for SNMP

remediation.command:
! To restrict SNMP to required interfaces issue the following command from the hierarchy;
set snmp interface <interface or interface list>

title: Recommend Accounting of Interactive Commands (where External AAA is used)
description: Where External AAA is used, Interactive Command Accounting Events should be sent to either TACACS+ or RADIUS. To protect any asset, including a Juniper router, you have to have a record of who logged in or attempted to login as well as who made changes to the configuration and when. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.1.4 Recommend Accounting of Interactive Commands (where External AAA is used)

remediation.command:
! Configure Accounting of Logins and Configuration Changes by entering the following commands under the hierarchy;
set system accounting events [change-log interactive-commands login] The interactive-commands should be selected at a minimum, although in many cases you may also wish to add change-log and login accounting.

title: Ensure external AAA is used
description: At least one external Authentication method should be specified. RADIUS and TACACS+ are centralized Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA) services. Both protocols provide services to authenticate users on routers, switches and other systems. Juniper routers support both RADIUS and TACACS+ authentication. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.3.1 Ensure external AAA is used

remediation.command:
! Configure at least one external Authentication method using the following commands under the hierarchy; For RADIUS
set system authentication-order radius For TACACS+
set system authentication-order tacplus For RADIUS then TACACS+
set system authentication-order [radius, tacplus] For TACACS+ then RADIUS
set system authentication-order [tacplus, radius]

title: Ensure Local Accounts can ONLY be used during loss of external AAA
description: Authentication using locally configured usernames and passwords should only be permitted when External AAA servers are down or cannot be reached. Juniper routers support local user accounts in addition to RADIUS and TACACS+ based authentication. JUNOS will use each of the configured protocols in order set under [edit system authentication-order] until the password is either accepted or the end of the ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.3.2 Ensure Local Accounts can ONLY be used during loss of external AAA

remediation.command:
! Remove local user authentication from the authentication order by issuing the following command from the hierarchy;
delete system authentication-order password This command will leave other authentication methods (RADIUS or TACACS+) that are already configured under the authentication-order statement.

title: Ensure Authentication is configured for Diagnostic Ports
description: An encrypted password should be set for access to the routers diagnostic ports. Most high end Juniper network devices contain Diagnostic Ports on one or more of the control boards installed in the system, such as FEB (Forwarding Engine Board) in M5 or M10 routers or SSB (System Switching Board) in M20 routers. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.4.1 Ensure Authentication is configured for Diagnostic Ports

remediation.command:
! Configure a password for the diagnostic ports using one of the following commands under the hierarchy; To enter a new password in plain text:
set system diag-port-authentication plain-text-password You will be prompted to enter the new password, which JUNOS will then hash with MD5 before placing the command in the candidate configuration. To enter an existing password hash which you have taken from an existing configuration file, type the following :
set system diag-port-authentication encrypted-password "<MD5 Hash>"

title: Ensure Diagnostic Port Authentication uses a complex password
description: A complex password should be used to protect access to Diagnostic Port/s. Due to the sensitivity of the routers Diagnostic Port/s a complex password should be employed to help prevent attackers employing 'brute force' or 'dictionary' attacks to gain access through these ports. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.4.2 Ensure Diagnostic Port Authentication uses a complex password

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Because Diagnostic Port passwords are automatically stored by JUNOS as a MD5 hash, which will always be 128bits long, it is not possible to confirm from the command line the complexity and length of the password used therefore this is not a scored item.

remediation.command:
! Configure a password for the diagnostic ports using one of the following commands under the hierarchy; To enter a new password in plain text :
set system diag-port-authentication plain-text-password You will be prompted to enter the new password, which JUNOS will then hash with MD5 before placing the command in the candidate configuration. To enter an existing password hash which you have taken from an existing configuration file, type the following :
set system diag-port-authentication encrypted-password "<MD5 Hash>"

title: Ensure Remote Login Class for Authorization through External AAA
description: External AAA servers should be utilized to provide Authorization via a single "Remote" template account. JUNOS routers ship with 4 Predefined Login Classes for user Authorization, these are: - super-user - read-only - operator - unauthorized These classes provide basic Authorization, restricting what users in each class can or cannot do, to allow organizations ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.7 Ensure Remote Login Class for Authorization through External AAA

remediation.command:
! To create a new class you can issue the following commands from the hierarchy. In this example, we create a new class named 'remote', granting only view permissions, and assign the remote user to the new class. More detailed permissions will be added to these permissions
set system login class remote permissions [ view ] (this class should also have Idle timeouts and other options set in line with other recommendations in this section). To change the class for a user account, use the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login user remote class remote A full discussion of RADIUS or TACACS+ configuration and options is beyond the scope of this guide, but a simple example of using a TACACS.net server running on Windows with AD integration for a remote user is shown below. This example is taken from an anonymized real world deployment, so also includes sections to allow access to different groups of TACACS+ Clients and permissions for Cisco IOS and Netscreen devices. The most relevant section is the <Service> for service=junos-exec, where the VSAs for TACACS+ Clients running JUNOS are defined, but the entire Authorization for this Class is given for context. <Authorization> <!--CIS Example remote user Authorization from TACACS.net Authorization.xml--> <UserGroups> <!-- The UserGroup is defined elsewhere - in this case it maps to an Active Directory Group call GRP-NETOPS --> <UserGroup>GRP-NETOPS</UserGroup> </UserGroups> <ClientGroups> <!--Defines the Groups of devices this usergroup can login to --> <ClientGroup>CORE-NET</ClientGroup>
! ... see the benchmark for the full procedure

title: Ensure local passwords require multiple character sets
description: Passwords for local user accounts must be configured to require character set changes. Weak passwords on local user accounts present a serious threat to the security of any device, allowing malicious user access through simple dictionary or brute force attacks. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.9 Ensure local passwords require multiple character sets

remediation.command:
! Configure a password character set changes using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login password change-type character-set

title: Ensure at least 4 set changes in local passwords
description: Passwords for local user accounts must be configured to require at least 4 character set changes. Weak passwords on local user accounts present a serious threat to the security of any device, allowing malicious user access through simple dictionary or brute force attacks. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.10 Ensure at least 4 set changes in local passwords

remediation.command:
! Configure the minimum character set changes using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login passwords minimum-changes 4

title: Ensure local passwords are at least 10 characters
description: Passwords for local user accounts must be configured to require at least 10 characters. Weak passwords on local user accounts present a serious threat to the security of the device, allowing malicious user access through simple dictionary or brute force attacks. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.11 Ensure local passwords are at least 10 characters

remediation.command:
! Configure the minimum characters for passwords using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login passwords minimum-length 8

title: Ensure SHA512 is used to hash local passwords
description: Passwords should be hashed with a strong hashing algorithm. Passwords for locally configured users are stored in the JUNOS configuration file. By applying a hashing algorithm to the password before storing it, JUNOS limits an attacker's ability to gain passwords from configuration backups or to escalate privileges ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.12 Ensure SHA512 is used to hash local passwords

remediation.command:
! Confirm that your device supports SHA-2 with 512bit hashes by issuing the following command from the hierarchy:
set system login password format ? The system should provide a range of options, such as in the example below which is for a system which does support SHA512:
set system login password format ? Possible completions: md5 Message Digest 5 sha1 Secure Hash Algorithm 1 sha256 Secure Hash Algorithm 256 ($5$) sha512 Secure Hash Algorithm 512 ($6$) Configure password hashing using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login login password format sha512 For systems which do not support SHA-2 with 512bit hashes, configure SHA-1 using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login login password format sha1 NOTE
- SHA1 hashing should only be configured on systems which do not support SHA512.

title: Ensure SSH Key Authentication is not set for User Logins
description: SSH Key Based Authentication should not be used for User Logins. Due to the sensitive nature of SSH, potentially allowing full management of the targeted device, protecting SSH access using strong authentication methods is essential to the security of the device. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.13 Ensure SSH Key Authentication is not set for User Logins

remediation.command:
! For each User Login configured with SSH Key based Authentication, you can delete the SSH Key with the following command from the hierarchy:
delete system login user <User ID> authentication The user can then be configured with a password locally or, inline with Recommendation 6.8.1 Ensure External AAA Server is set , leave the authentication method blank and allow the External AAA to control Authentication. Alternatively, you may wish to delete the local user account entirely using the following command:
delete system login user <User ID>

title: Ensure Multi-Factor is used with External AAA
description: Multi-factor Authentication should be used for management sessions. Even with the password complexity restrictions and use of External AAA servers for centralized control of user Authentication, login with usernames and passwords is commonly exploited through Phishing, Brute Force or other methods. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.14 Ensure Multi-Factor is used with External AAA

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Verify that: Multi-factor Authentication should be used for management sessions

remediation.command: ! Follow the remediation procedure in the benchmark: Ensure Multi-Factor is used with External AAA

title: Ensure Authentication Keys are used for all NTP Servers
description: Authentication keys should be set for NTP Servers. Having established the need for NTP, it is essential to ensure that the devices time is not manipulated by an attacker as this could allow DoS to services relying on accurate time as well as replay attacks and other malicious activity. Fails if any 'set system ntp server' line has no 'key <id>'. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.7.5 Ensure Authentication Keys are used for all NTP Servers

title: Ensure Different Authentication Keys for each NTP Server
description: Different authentication keys should be set for each NTP Server. Having established the need for NTP, it is essential to ensure that the devices time is not manipulated by an attacker as this could allow DoS to services relying on accurate time as well as replay attacks and other malicious activity. Not reliably checkable from an exported configuration. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.7.6 Ensure Different Authentication Keys for each NTP Server

audit.command: Not reliably checkable from an exported configuration. From the command prompt, execute the following command: [edit] user@host#show system ntp | match "server|key" The above command should return each of the configured NTP Servers for the JUNOS Device, as well as configured and trusted keys. The following conditions must all be met: - Every server has a 'key ' configured - Each server uses a different '' - A corresponding 'authentication-key' is configured for each 'key ' - Each 'authentication-key' used with a server is included in the 'trusted-key' list

remediation.command:
! Keys are configured on a key ring and identified by an ID number. To add a key enter the following commands from the hierarchy:
set system ntp authentication-key <Key ID> type <algorithm> value <Key>
set system ntp trusted-key <Key ID> Set the keys for all configured NTP servers using the following commands under the hierarchy:
set system ntp server <Servers IP> key <key ID> If this device is operating as an NTP Server and has clients which use different keys or algorithms, these can be set with the peer option:
set system ntp peer <Peers IP> key <key ID> NOTE
- The Key ID must also be listed in the trusted-key list to be accepted.

title: Ensure Strong Authentication Methods are used for NTP Authentication
description: Strong authentication methods should be set for NTP Servers. Having established the need for NTP, it is essential to ensure that the devices time is not manipulated by an attacker as this could allow DoS to services relying on accurate time as well as replay attacks and other malicious activity. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.7.7 Ensure Strong Authentication Methods are used for NTP Authentication

title: Ensure External AAA Server is set
description: At least one external Authentication server should be configured. RADIUS and TACACS+ are centralized Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA) services. Both protocols provide services to Authenticate users on routers, switches and other systems. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.8.1 Ensure External AAA Server is set

remediation.command:
! Configure at least one External Authentication Server using the following commands under the hierarchy; For RADIUS
set system radius-server <server ip> secret <shared secret> source-address <loopback IP> For TACACS+
set system tacplus-server <server ip> secret <shared secret> source-address <loopback IP> NOTE - the source-address is generally set as the Loopback, but for some environments the Fxp0.0/out of band interface may be used, or another interface preferred.

title: Ensure Share-Secret is set for External AAA Servers
description: External AAA Servers should be configured with a Shared Secret. RADIUS and TACACS+ are centralized Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA) services. Both protocols provide services to authenticate users on routers, switches and other systems. Approximation: fails if TACACS+/RADIUS servers are defined but none of that type has a secret. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.8.2 Ensure Share-Secret is set for External AAA Servers

remediation.command:
! Configure a Shared Secret for all External Authentication Server using the following commands under the hierarchy; For RADIUS Servers:
set system radius-server <server ip> secret <shared secret> For TACACS+ Servers:
set system tacplus-server <server ip> secret <shared secret>

title: Ensure a Different Shared Secret is Set for each External AAA Server
description: External AAA Servers should be configured with a Shared Secret. RADIUS and TACACS+ are centralized Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA) services. Both protocols provide services to Authenticate and Authorization of users on routers, switches and other systems. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.8.3 Ensure a Different Shared Secret is Set for each External AAA Server

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Because the Shared Secrets are stored as salted hashed values in the JUNOS configuration, it is not possible to readily audit this Recommendation from the JUNOS device, so this Recommendation is not Scored.

remediation.command:
! Configure a Shared Secret for all External Authentication Server using the following commands under the hierarchy; For RADIUS
set system radius-server <server ip> secret <shared secret> source-address <loopback IP> For TACACS+
set system tacplus-server <server ip> secret <shared secret> source-address <Loopback IP>

title: Ensure MS-CHAPv2 RADIUS Authentication
description: MS-CHAPv2 should be used for RADIUS authentication if RADIUS Servers are configured. RADIUS is a centralized Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA) protocol providing services to authenticate users on routers, switches and other systems. Passes when no RADIUS server is configured. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.8.4 Ensure MS-CHAPv2 RADIUS Authentication

remediation.command:
! Configure RADIUS to use MS-CHAPv2 Authentication using the following commands under the hierarchy;
set system radius-options password-protocol mschap-v2

title: Ensure Source-Address is set for External AAA Servers
description: The Source-Address should be set for each External AAA Server configured. RADIUS and TACACS+ are centralized Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA) services. Both protocols provide services to Authenticate users on routers, switches and other systems. Approximation: fails if TACACS+/RADIUS servers are defined but none of that type has a source-address. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.8.5 Ensure Source-Address is set for External AAA Servers

remediation.command:
! Configure at least one External Authentication Server using the following commands under the hierarchy; For RADIUS
set system radius-server <server ip> secret <shared secret> source-address <loopback IP> Or for TACACS+
set system tacplus-server <server ip> secret <shared secret> source-address <loopback IP>

title: Ensure a complex Root Password is Set
description: A complex Root Password should be set for the system. Due to the importance of the Root user account, which has full control of the JUNOS system and underlying Unix OS, a complex password should be employed to help prevent attackers employing 'brute force' or 'dictionary' attacks to gain full control of the ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.9.1 Ensure a complex Root Password is Set

remediation.command:
! Root Authentication must be configured prior to the first commit on a new system. A Root password may be set from the CLI using either of the two methods below, from the hierarchy. To enter a new Root Password in plain text type:
set system root-authentication plain-text-password You will be prompted to enter the new Password twice and, if the Passwords match, JUNOS will add a SHA1 hash of the Password to the configuration. Alternatively, if you are copying the configuration from an existing JUNOS system (using the same hashing algorithm) or template, you may apply an existing hash of the Root password:
set system root-authentication encrypted-password "<hash>"

title: Ensure Root Password is Unique
description: The Root Password should be unique. Due to the rights associated with the Root user account it must be protected at all costs to prevent malicious users taking ownership of the router. Using the same password for an individual User or other usage exposes the extremely privileged Root user ... CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.9.2 Ensure Root Password is Unique

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Because all Root Passwords are automatically stored by JUNOS as a SHA1 hash, which will always be 160bits long, it is not possible to confirm the uniqueness of the Root Password.

remediation.command:
! Users will generally be prompted to set the Root password during initial setup of the router, however, a password may be set from the CLI using either of the two methods below from the hierarchy; To enter a new Root Password in plain text type:
set system root-authentication plain-text-password You will be prompted to enter the new Password twice and, if the Passwords match, JUNOS will add a SHA1 hash of the Password to the configuration. If you already have a SHA1 hash of your Root Password (from an existing router configuration, for example), enter the following command:
set system root-authentication encrypted-password "<SHA1 hash>" If JWEB is installed on your router, the Root Password may also be changed through the Configuration > Quick Configuration > Setup page.

title: Ensure SSH Key Authentication is not set for Root Login
description: SSH Key Based Authentication should not be used for Root Login. Due to the sensitive nature of SSH, potentially allowing full management of the targeted device, protecting SSH access using strong authentication methods is essential to the security of the device. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.9.3 Ensure SSH Key Authentication is not set for Root Login

remediation.command:
! If SSH Key based Authentication is configured for the Root Authentication, remove it using the following command from the hierarchy:
delete system root-authentication To set a new Root Password in plain text type:
set system root-authentication plain-text-password You will be prompted to enter the new Password twice and, if the Passwords match, JUNOS will add a hash of the Password to the configuration. If you already have a hash of your Root Password (from an existing router configuration, for example), enter the following command:
set system root-authentication encrypted-password "<hash>" Note
- Hashes use SHA1 by default, but may use other hashing mechanisms depending on the device configuration - ensure the device you are copying from is configured to use the same hashing method. If JWEB is installed on your router, the Root Password may also be changed through the Configuration > Quick Configuration > Setup page.

title: Ensure SSH Service is Configured if Remote CLI is Required
description: SSH should be utilized for remote console sessions to Juniper routers. SSH provides administrators with a remote console session on the router in a similar fashion to Telnet. Unlike Telnet, SSH encrypts all data as it transits the network and ensures the identity of the remote host. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.1.1 Ensure SSH Service is Configured if Remote CLI is Required

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. From the command prompt, execute the following command: [edit] user@host#show system services | match "ssh {" | count This command should return a line count of 1 if SSH is configured.

remediation.command:
! To enable SSH access issue the following command from the hierarchy:
set system services ssh Where SSH is used, all other Recommendations in this section should be considered. If SSH is currently configured but is not required it should be disabled using the following command from the hierarchy:
delete system services ssh

title: Ensure SSH is Restricted to Version 2
description: Remote console connections should only use SSH Version 2. SSH Version 1 has been subject to a number of serious vulnerabilities and is no longer considered to be a secure protocol, resulting in the adoption of SSH Version 2 as an Internet Standard in 2006. Recent Junos releases only support SSHv2 and no longer show this statement. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.1.2 Ensure SSH is Restricted to Version 2

remediation.command:
! To restrict SSH to Version 2 only, issue the following command from the hierarchy:
set system services ssh protocol-version v2

title: Ensure SSH Connection Limit is Set
description: SSH connections should be limited. SSH is a common management protocol, so is often targeted by attackers trying to gain access to routers or execute Denial of Service (DoS) attacks. To limit the effectiveness of DoS and Brute Force attacks targeting the JUNOS device using the SSH service the ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.1.3 Ensure SSH Connection Limit is Set

remediation.command:
! To restrict concurrent SSH connections, issue the following command from the hierarchy:
set system services ssh connection-limit <limit> NOTE
- On some platforms the maximum configuration connection limit may be significantly lower than 10, for example, on an SRX110 the connection limit can be set to a value between 1 and 3.

title: Ensure SSH Rate Limit is Configured
description: SSH connections should be limited. SSH is a common management protocol, so is often targeted by attackers trying to gain access to routers or execute Denial of Service (DoS) attacks. To limit the effectiveness of DoS and Brute Force attacks targeting the JUNOS Device using the SSH service, ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.1.4 Ensure SSH Rate Limit is Configured

remediation.command:
! To restrict concurrent SSH connections, issue the following command from the hierarchy;
set system services ssh rate-limit <limit>

title: Ensure Remote Root-Login is denied via SSH
description: Prevent remote access to the Root user account on the device. During normal operation, remote access to the Root user should not be required. Because the Root user account has full access to the router and underlying BSD OS it is an extremely valuable target for attackers and must be protected from remote exploitation. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.1.5 Ensure Remote Root-Login is denied via SSH

remediation.command:
! To disable remote access to the Root account issue the following command from the hierarchy:
set system services ssh root-login deny

title: Ensure Strong Ciphers are set for SSH
description: SSH should be configured with strong ciphers. SSH (Secure Shell) is the defacto standard protocol used for remote administration of network devices and Unix servers, providing an encrypted and authenticated alternative to Telnet. Fails if ciphers are not restricted or a cipher without aes/3des is configured (per the PDF audit). Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.1.6 Ensure Strong Ciphers are set for SSH

remediation.command:
! To remove a single insecure cipher, issue the following command from the hierarchy;
delete system services ssh ciphers <cipher suite name> If multiple insecure Ciphers were set, it will generally be easier to delete all the Cipher restrictions with the following command:
delete system services ssh ciphers Once all insecure Ciphers have been removed, add one or more stronger Ciphers (in this example all stronger Ciphers available on most JUNOS devices are set in a single command)
set system services ssh ciphers [ 3des-cbc aes128-cbc aes128-ctr aes128-gcm@openssh.com aes192-cbc aes192-ctr aes256-cbc aes256-ctr aes256-gcm@openssh.com ] Note - note all of the Ciphers in the example above are supported on all JUNOS devices. In many cases the GCM mode AES ciphers may be unavailable, a shorter list of Ciphers may be set with the following command for these systems:
set system services ssh ciphers [ 3des-cbc aes128-cbc aes128-ctr aes192-cbc aes192-ctr aes256-cbc aes256-ctr ] Finally, single Ciphers or a smaller selection of these more secure Ciphers may be selected on the user's discretion.
set system services ssh ciphers <cipher suite name>

title: Ensure Only Suite B Ciphers are set for SSH
description: SSH should be configured with Ciphers based on the Suite B Standard. SSH (Secure Shell) is the defacto standard protocol used for remote administration of network devices and Unix servers, providing an encrypted and authenticated alternative to Telnet. Fails if ciphers are not restricted or any non-GCM cipher is configured. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.1.7 Ensure Only Suite B Ciphers are set for SSH

remediation.command:
! To remove a single insecure cipher, issue the following command from the hierarchy;
delete system services ssh ciphers <cipher suite name> If multiple insecure Ciphers were set, it will generally be easier to delete all the Cipher restrictions with the following command:
delete system services ssh ciphers Once all insecure Ciphers have been removed, add one or more of the AES-GCM ciphers.
set system services ssh ciphers [ aes128-gcm@openssh.com aes256-gcm@openssh.com ]

title: Ensure Strong MACs are set for SSH
description: SSH should be configured with strong message authentication algorithms. SSH (Secure Shell) is the defacto standard protocol used for remote administration of network devices and Unix servers, providing an encrypted and authenticated alternative to Telnet. Fails if MACs are not restricted or a non-SHA2 MAC is configured. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.1.8 Ensure Strong MACs are set for SSH

remediation.command:
! To remove a single insecure MAC method, issue the following command from the hierarchy;
delete system services ssh macs <mac name> If multiple insecure MAC methods were set, it will generally be easier to delete all the MAC method restrictions with the following command:
delete system services ssh macs Once all insecure MAC methods have been removed, add one or more stronger MACS (in this example all stronger MACS available on most JUNOS devices are set in a single command)
set system services ssh macs [ hmac-sha2-256 hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com hmac-sha2-512 hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com ] Finally, single MAC methods or a smaller selection of these more secure MACs may be selected on the users discretion.
set system services ssh macs <mac name>

title: Ensure Strong Key Exchange Methods are set for SSH
description: SSH should be configured with strong key exchange algorithms. SSH (Secure Shell) is the defacto standard protocol used for remote administration of network devices and Unix servers, providing an encrypted and authenticated alternative to Telnet. Fails if key exchange is not restricted or a SHA-1 based method is configured. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.1.9 Ensure Strong Key Exchange Methods are set for SSH

remediation.command:
! To remove a single insecure Key Exchange method, issue the following command from the hierarchy;
delete system services ssh key-exchange <mac name> If multiple insecure Key Exchange methods were set, it will generally be easier to delete all the Key Exchange method restrictions with the following command:
delete system services ssh key-exchange Once all insecure methods have been removed, add one or more stronger Key Exchange methods (in this example all stronger methods available on most JUNOS devices are set in a single command)
set system services ssh key-exchange [ curve25519-sha256 ecdh-sha2-nistp256 ecdh-sha2-nistp384 ecdh-sha2-nistp521 group-exchange-sha2 ] Finally, single Key Exchange methods or a smaller selection of these more secure methods may be selected on the user's discretion.
set system services ssh key-exchange <method>

title: Ensure Only Suite B Key Exchange Methods are set for SSH
description: SSH should be configured to use only Suite B key exchange algorithms. SSH (Secure Shell) is the defacto standard protocol used for remote administration of network devices and Unix servers, providing an encrypted and authenticated alternative to Telnet. Fails if key exchange is not restricted or a non-NIST (non Suite B) method is configured. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.1.10 Ensure Only Suite B Key Exchange Methods are set for SSH

remediation.command:
! To remove a single non-Suite B Key Exchange method, issue the following command from the hierarchy;
delete system services ssh key-exchange <mac name> If multiple insecure Key Exchange methods were set, it will generally be easier to delete all the Key Exchange method restrictions with the following command:
delete system services ssh key-exchange Once all insecure methods have been removed, add one or more stronger Key Exchange methods (in this example all Suite B methods available on most JUNOS devices are set in a single command)
set system services ssh key-exchange [ ecdh-sha2-nistp256 ecdh-sha2-nistp384 ecdh-sha2-nistp512 ] NOTE
- The ecdh-sha2-nistp512 Key Exchange method is not cited specifically in RFC6239, but is acceptable in addition/in place of the other NIST Elliptic Curve Diffie Hellman exchange methods for the purposes of this recommendation. Finally, single Key Exchange methods or a smaller selection of these more secure methods may be selected on the user's discretion.
set system services ssh key-exchange <method>

title: Ensure Strong Key Signing Algorithms are set for SSH
description: SSH should be configured with strong key signing algorithms. SSH (Secure Shell) is the defacto standard protocol used for remote administration of network devices and Unix servers, providing an encrypted and authenticated alternative to Telnet. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.1.11 Ensure Strong Key Signing Algorithms are set for SSH

remediation.command:
! To explicitly disable DSA signatures, type the following command at the hierarchy:
set system services ssh hostkey-algorithm no-ssh-dss Enable one or more stronger ciphers using the following commands:
set system services ssh hostkey-algorithm ssh-ecdsa
set system services ssh hostkey-algorithm ssh-ed25519
set system services ssh hostkey-algorithm ssh-rsa

title: Ensure Only Suite B Based Key Signing Algorithms are set for SSH
description: SSH should be configured with Suite B based key signing algorithms. SSH (Secure Shell) is the defacto standard protocol used for remote administration of network devices and Unix servers, providing an encrypted and authenticated alternative to Telnet. Requires no-ssh-dss, no-ssh-rsa and no-ssh-ed25519. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.1.12 Ensure Only Suite B Based Key Signing Algorithms are set for SSH

remediation.command:
! To explicitly disable DSA, RSA and ED25519 signatures, type the following commands at the hierarchy:
set system services ssh hostkey-algorithm no-ssh-dss
set system services ssh hostkey-algorithm no-ssh-rsa
set system services ssh hostkey-algorithm no-ssh-ed25519 Enable ECDSA for SSH Public Keys using the following commands:
set system services ssh hostkey-algorithm ssh-ecdsa

title: Ensure SSH Key Authentication is Disabled
description: SSH Key based Authentication should be disabled (if not used for automation).
