description: NDP should be protected. One of the primary functions of NDP is to resolve Network Layer (IP) addresses to Link Layer (eg Ethernet) addresses, a function performed in IPv4 by ARP. An attacker who has access to the broadcast segment may abuse NDP or ARP to trick hosts into sending the ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.9.1 Ensure Secure Neighbor Discovery is configured

remediation.command:
! If you have deployed IPv6 you can configure SEND by issuing the following commands from the hierarchy: If you have not already done so, you will need to generate or install an RSA key pair, to generate a new pair enter the following command:
request pki generate-key-pair <name> <ca-profile> Next, set the security level to define how unsecure NDP messages should be handled. If only a subset of devices will be configured to use SEND, then use the default option. If all nodes on the segment require protection, which is recommended, use the secure-messages-only option:
set protocols neighbor-discovery secure security-level secure-messages-only Finally, specify the key pair and details you generated/installed earlier:
set protocols neighbor-discovery secure cryptographic-address key-pair <name>
set protocols neighbor-discovery secure cryptographic-address key-length <length> For more details on configuring Public/Private Key Pairs in JUNOS please refer to: Generating a Public-Private Key Pair, JUNOS Software Security Configuration Guide, Juniper Networks

title: Ensure ICMP Router Discovery is disabled
description: ICMP Router Discovery should not be used. ICMP Router Discovery provides details of routers attached to a broadcast or multicast segment in response to Router Solicitation messages from hosts or in the form of a period Router Advertisement. Passes when router-discovery is not configured (disabled by default). Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.10.1 Ensure ICMP Router Discovery is disabled

remediation.command:
! If you have configured ICMP Router Discovery and do not require it, you can disable it by issuing the following command from the hierarchy:
set protocols router-discovery disable

title: Ensure LLDP is Disabled if not Required
description: LLDP should be disabled when not required. The Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) is a vendor-neutral and widely supported standard used for network devices to advertise information about their capabilities, identity, software and management details to other network devices on the LAN. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.12.1 Ensure LLDP is Disabled if not Required

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Due to the range of options as to the type of device, deployment scenario and where LLDP will be used in the network, it is not possible to provide Automated Scoring of this recommendation. To check whether LLDP is enabled, use the following command from the [edit protocols] configuration hierarchy: [edit protocols] user@host#show lldp | display set | match "interface|disable" The command should return all Routing Instances or Logical Systems where LLDP has been enabled globally for all interfaces by returning one or more lines ...

remediation.command:
! To turn off LLDP globally for all interfaces, issue the following command from the configuration hierarchy:
set protocols lldp disable Sending of LLDPDUs will be disabled, while any LLDP related configuration will be retained (but ignored). Alternatively, you may wish to disable LLDP on a per-interface basis by issuing the following command from the configuration hierarchy: To disable LLDP for a specific interface, leaving LLDP enabled for all others:
set protocols lldp interface <interface name> disable Or to disable LLDP for all interfaces and allow only for specific ports:
delete protocols lldp interface all
set protocols lldp interface <interface name> This procedure should be repeated for all Routing Instances/Logical Systems where LLDP is configured but not required.

title: Ensure LLDP-MED is Disabled if not Required
description: LLDP-MED should be disabled when not required. The Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) is a vendor-neutral and widely supported standard used for network devices to advertise information about their capabilities, identity, software and management details to other network devices on the LAN. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.12.2 Ensure LLDP-MED is Disabled if not Required

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Due to the range of options as to the type of device, deployment scenario and where LLDP will be used in the network, it is not possible to provide Automated Scoring of this recommendation. To check whether LLDP is enabled, use the following command from the [edit protocols] configuration hierarchy: [edit protocols] user@host#show lldp-med | display set | match "interface|disable" LLDP-MED is enabled by default on EX series platforms, so will be enabled for all Interfaces if set protocols lldp-med interface all disable is not ...

remediation.command:
! To turn off LLDP-MED globally for all interfaces, issue the following command from the configuration hierarchy:
set protocols lldp-med interface all disable Sending of LLDPDUs will be disabled, while any other LLDP-MED related configuration will be retained (but ignored). Alternatively, you may wish to disable LLDP on a per-interface basis by issuing the following command from the configuration hierarchy: To disable LLDP-MED for a specific interface, leaving LLDP-MED enabled for all others:
set protocols lldp-med interface <interface name> disable Or to disable LLDP-MED for all interfaces and allow only for specific ports:
set protocols lldp-med interface all disable
set protocols lldp-med interface <interface name> This procedure should be repeated for all Routing Instances/Logical Systems where LLDP-MED is configured but not required.

title: Ensure SNMPv1/2 are set to Read Only
description: Do not allow Read-Write SNMP access for versions below SNMPv3. SNMP can be used to read and write configuration information from a router using your Network Management Systems; however the inherently insecure design of the older SNMP V1, V2 and V2C standards, which do not use encryption to protect community strings, make ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2 Ensure SNMPv1/2 are set to Read Only

title: Ensure a client list is set for SNMPv1/v2 communities
description: Limit clients to access SNMP. Even when limited to read only access, SNMP can provide an attacker with a wealth of information about your router and network topology. To limit the potential for attacks against your routers SNMP service you should limit the IP addresses that are permitted ... Passes when no SNMP community exists; otherwise requires a client-list (or clients) restriction. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.3 Ensure a client list is set for SNMPv1/v2 communities

remediation.command:
! To configure a client list issue the following command under the hierarchy;
edit snmp client-list <client list name>
set snmp client-list <client list name> default restrict
set snmp client-list <client list name> <ip address/range>
set snmp client-list <client list name> <ip address> restrict #optionally add exceptions
up 1
edit snmp community <community name>
set snmp community <community name> client-list-name <community name> The set default restrict is covered in detail in the next recommendation. Additional IP Addresses may be permitted by repeating the set <ip address/range> command as needed. Optionally, addresses that you wish to deny from within a permitted range previously set can be configured with the set <ip address> restrict command. Note
- Client-lists may also be defined directly under the hierarchy for use within the specified community with the same effect, but for ease of management and audit, the first method is preferred.

title: Ensure AES128 is set for all SNMPv3 users
description: Do not allow plaintext SNMPv3 access. SNMPv3 provides much improved security over previous versions by offering options for Authentication and Encryption of messages. When configuring a user for SNMPv3 you have the option of using a range of encryption schemes, or no encryption at all, to protect ... Passes when no SNMPv3 user exists; fails on DES/3DES/none privacy or when no user uses privacy-aes128. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.6 Ensure AES128 is set for all SNMPv3 users

remediation.command:
! For each SNMPv3 user created on your router add privacy options by issuing the following command from the hierarchy;
set snmp v3 usm local-engine user <username> privacy-aes128 privacy-password <password>

title: Ensure SNMP is set to OOB management only
description: SNMP should only be configured on Out of Band management interfaces. By default the SNMP service will listen for incoming connections on all interfaces which have an IP Address configured, exposing SNMP to users on all networks through which the router is reachable. Fails if SNMP is configured without interface restriction or is bound to a non out-of-band interface (fxp/em/me/jmgmt). Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.9 Ensure SNMP is set to OOB management only

title: Ensure Accounting Destination is configured
description: Where external Authentication, Authorization and Accounting services using either RADIUS or TACACS+ are used, accounting data should be sent to at least one AAA server destination. RADIUS and TACACS+ are centralized Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA) services. Both protocols provide services to receive and record information about what users and processes on a router are doing. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.1.1 Ensure Accounting Destination is configured

remediation.command:
! Configure one or more RADIUS or TACACS+ servers as Accounting Destinations use the following commands under the hierarchy; For RADIUS
set system accounting destination radius server <server ip> secret <shared secret> For TACACS+
set system accounting destination tacplus server <server ip> secret <shared secret>

title: Ensure Accounting of Logins
description: When External AAA is used, Login Events should be sent to configured accounting destinations. To protect any asset, including a Juniper router, you have to have a record of who logged in or attempted to login as well as who made changes to the configuration and when. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.1.2 Ensure Accounting of Logins

remediation.command:
! Configure Accounting of Logins and Configuration Changes by entering the following commands under the hierarchy;
set system accounting events login

title: Ensure Accounting of Configuration Changes
description: When External AAA is used Configuration Change events should be sent to configured accounting destinations. To protect any asset, including a Juniper router, an audit trail of changes made to the devices configuration, when they were made and by whom is essential. JUNOS can log these events to RADIUS and/or TACACS+ servers to allow reliable, centralized records to ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.1.3 Ensure Accounting of Configuration Changes

remediation.command:
! Configure Accounting of Logins and Configuration Changes by entering the following commands under the hierarchy;
set system accounting events change-log

title: Ensure Archive on Commit
description: The routers configuration should be archived whenever changes are committed. Before changes made to a JUNOS router are applied they must be committed. Archiving the configuration to an external server on every commit creates a complete history of all changes allowing an effective 'post mortem' to be carried out following any breach ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.2.1 Ensure Archive on Commit

remediation.command:
! To enable Archival on commit issue the following commands from the hierarchy;
set system archival configuration transfer-on-commit

title: Ensure at least one SCP Archive Site is configured
description: Configuration archival should use only secure transport over SCP. Archiving the configuration to an external server creates a history of changes allowing an effective 'post mortem' to be carried out following any breach and aiding recovery to security and other incidents. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.2.2 Ensure at least one SCP Archive Site is configured

remediation.command:
! To enable a Secure Copy Archival Site on commit issue the following commands from the hierarchy;
set system archival configuration archive-site <SCP URL> password <password>

title: Ensure NO Plain Text Archive Sites are configured
description: The routers configuration MUST NOT be sent in plain text to the Archive Site. JUNOS routers can use a range of protocols for copying configuration files to Archive Sites including FTP, TFTP, NFS and SCP. Of these, only Secure Copy (SCP) provides encryption for the data in transit. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.2.3 Ensure NO Plain Text Archive Sites are configured

remediation.command:
! Archival is not configured by default. If plain text Archive Sites have been configured, they can be removed by issuing the following command from the hierarchy;
delete system archival configuration archive-site <URL> Archive sites should be reconfigured using SCP.

title: Ensure ICMPv4 rate-limit is Set
description: ICMPv4 traffic should be rate limited to protect the devices resources. Many Denial of Service attacks against network devices will attempt to overwhelm the target's processing, memory or bandwidth by barraging the router with malicious ICMP traffic which may be easily spoofed or generated in significant volumes. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.5.1 Ensure ICMPv4 rate-limit is Set

remediation.command:
! ICMPv4 Rate Limiting can be configured by issuing the following commands from the hierarchy.
set system internet-options icmpv4-rate-limit bucket-size <bucket> packet-limit <limit> Where: - <bucket> is the size of the Rate Limit Bucket, in seconds (if not specified, defaults to 5 seconds) - <limit> is the rate at which packets are added to the bucket, in packets per second (if not specified, defaults to 1000pps)

title: Ensure ICMPv6 rate-limit is Set
description: ICMPv6 traffic should be rate limited to protect the devices resources. Many Denial of Service attacks against network devices will attempt to overwhelm the target's processing, memory or bandwidth by barraging the router with malicious ICMP traffic which may be easily spoofed or generated in significant volumes. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.5.2 Ensure ICMPv6 rate-limit is Set

remediation.command:
! ICMPv6 Rate Limiting can be configured by issuing the following commands from the hierarchy.
set system internet-options icmpv6-rate-limit bucket <bucket> limit <limit> Where: - is the size of the Rate Limit Bucket, in seconds (if not specified, defaults to 5 seconds) - is the rate at which packets are added to the bucket, in packets per second (if not specified, defaults to 1000pps)

title: Ensure ICMP Source-Quench is Set to Disabled
description: ICMP Source Quench messages should be ignored. ICMP Source Quench messages are intended to allow a host to request that a peer with which it is communicating slows down the transmission of new data because the host is being overwhelmed. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.5.3 Ensure ICMP Source-Quench is Set to Disabled

remediation.command:
! Configure the JUNOS Device to ignore ICMP source-quench messages by issuing the following command from the hierarchy.
set system internet-options no-source-quench

title: Ensure TCP SYN/FIN is Set to Drop
description: TCP Segments which have both the SYN and FIN flags set should be dropped. TCP packets that have both SYN and FIN flags set are sometimes used by attackers to bypass Intrusion Detection Systems and Firewalls or to directly attack hosts on the target network. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.5.4 Ensure TCP SYN/FIN is Set to Drop

remediation.command:
! Configure the router to drop TCP Segments containing both SYN and FIN flags by issuing the following command from the hierarchy.
set system internet-options tcp-drop-synfin-set

title: Ensure TCP RST is Set to Disabled
description: Connection attempts to a closed / non-listening port should not return a TCP RST. As with most Operating Systems, by default, when a client attempts to connect to a TCP port which is not being used by a service to listen for connections JUNOS will return a TCP RST message to inform the client that there is no service available on that ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.5.5 Ensure TCP RST is Set to Disabled

remediation.command:
! To disable sending TCP RSTs to any connections to closed ports issue the following command from the hierarchy.
set system internet-options no-tcp-reset drop-all-tcp

title: Ensure Max 3 Failed Login Attempts
description: A maximum of 3 failed login attempts should be allowed before the session is disconnected. Remote administration protocols like Telnet and SSH are commonly targeted by Brute Force or Dictionary attacks where a malicious user attempts to guess a valid username/password combination in order to gain control of the router. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.1.1 Ensure Max 3 Failed Login Attempts

remediation.command:
! Configure the number of tried before disconnect using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login retry-options tries-before-disconnect

title: Ensure Max Login Backoff Threshold of 2
description: A maximum of 2 failed login should trigger a backoff. Remote administration protocols like Telnet and SSH are commonly targeted by Brute Force or Dictionary attacks where a malicious user attempts to guess a valid username/password combination in order to gain control of the router. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.1.2 Ensure Max Login Backoff Threshold of 2

remediation.command:
! Configure the backoff threshold using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login retry-options backoff-threshold <threshold>

title: Ensure Minimum Backoff Factor of 5
description: A minimum of 5 seconds should be used for the backoff factor. Remote administration protocols like Telnet and SSH are commonly targeted by Brute Force or Dictionary attacks where a malicious user attempts to guess a valid username/password combination in order to gain control of the router. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.1.3 Ensure Minimum Backoff Factor of 5

remediation.command:
! Configure the backoff threshold using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login retry-options backoff-factor

title: Ensure Minimum Session Time of at least 20 seconds
description: A Minimum Session Time should be set to at least 20 seconds. Remote administration protocols like Telnet and SSH are commonly targeted by Brute Force or Dictionary attacks where a malicious user attempts to guess a valid username/password combination in order to gain control of the router. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.1.4 Ensure Minimum Session Time of at least 20 seconds

remediation.command:
! Configure the Minimum Session Time using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login retry-options minimum-time

title: Ensure Lockout-period is set to at least 30 minutes
description: Users who have been disconnected due to bad login attempts should be locked out for 30 minutes. Remote administration protocols like Telnet and SSH are commonly targeted by Brute Force or Dictionary attacks where a malicious user attempts to guess a valid username/password combination in order to gain control of the router. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.1.5 Ensure Lockout-period is set to at least 30 minutes

remediation.command:
! Configure the time users should be locked out using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login retry-options lockout-period 30

title: Ensure Login Class is set for all Users Accounts
description: All user accounts must have a class set. Controlling the level of access which users are granted when logging into a router, helps protect against both malicious attacks and accidental misconfiguration of the router by less experienced staff. Approximation without per-user correlation: fails if users exist but no 'class' line is configured for any of them. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.2 Ensure Login Class is set for all Users Accounts

remediation.command:
! Configure a class for a user account using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login user <username> class <class name>

title: Ensure Idle Timeout is set for all Login Classes
description: All login classes should have an idle timeout defined. Controlling the level of access which users are granted when logging into a router, helps protect against both malicious attacks and accidental misconfiguration of the router by less experienced staff. Fails if a class sets idle-timeout above 15 (or 0), or classes exist but none sets an idle-timeout. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.3 Ensure Idle Timeout is set for all Login Classes

remediation.command:
! Configure the Idle Timeout for a class using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login class <class name> idle-timeout <timeout in minutes>

title: Ensure Custom Login Classes have Permissions Defined
description: All login classes should have permissions defined. Controlling the level of access which users are granted when logging into a router, helps protect against both malicious attacks and accidental misconfiguration of the router by less experienced staff. Approximation: fails if custom classes exist but none defines permissions. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.4 Ensure Custom Login Classes have Permissions Defined

remediation.command:
! Configure the Permissions for a class using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login class <class name> permissions <permission or list of permissions>

title: Ensure all Custom Login Classes Forbid Shell Access
description: All login classes should deny Shell access. JUNOS runs on top of a heavily modified BSD Unix based operating system and users with certain permission sets will be able to start a Shell to interact with this underlying system directly. Approximation: fails if custom classes exist but none has a deny-commands entry (verify it contains "start shell"). Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.5 Ensure all Custom Login Classes Forbid Shell Access

remediation.command:
! Deny Shell access for a class using the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login class <class name> deny-commands "start shell" You may also wish to deny other commands or groups of commands by using a list or Regular Expression as the deny-commands value, ensure that start shell is still included.

title: Ensure Predefined Login Classes are not used
description: All user accounts must have a class set, but the Predefined JUNOS Login Classes should be avoided. JUNOS routers ship with 4 Predefined Login Classes, these are: - super-user - read-only - operator - unauthorized These classes provide basic configuration to allow organizations to get a router up and running, but do not provide fine grained control needed ... Allows one emergency account in a predefined class; fails if two or more users use predefined classes. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.6.6 Ensure Predefined Login Classes are not used

audit.pattern: (?m)(?s:^set system login user \S+ class (?:super-user|superuser|read-only|operator|unauthorized)\b.*^set system login user \S+ class (?:super-user|superuser|read-only|operator|unauthorized)\b)

remediation.command:
! To create a new class you can issue the following commands from the hierarchy. In this example, we create a new class named 'noc' and allow them permissions to run show commands like show bgp summary, view the configuration and access the network with ping, SSH, traceroute and Telnet.
set system login class noc permissions [ view view-configuration network ] (this class should also have Idle timeouts and other options set in line with other recommendations in this section). To change the class for a user account, use the following command under the hierarchy:
set system login user <username> class <class name>

title: Ensure External NTP Servers are set
description: At least one, and preferably three or more, external NTP Servers should be configured. Keeping time settings consistent across a network is vital if log data is to be meaningful and usable in understanding faults and security incidents. Consistent time settings are also fundamental to the operation of some network protocols and services such as ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.7.1 Ensure External NTP Servers are set

remediation.command:
! Configure at least one External NTP Server using the following commands under the hierarchy;
set system ntp server <Servers IP>

title: Ensure Multiple External NTP Servers are set
description: At least 3 External NTP Servers should be set. Keeping time settings consistent across a network is vital if log data is to be meaningful and usable in understanding faults and security incidents. Consistent time settings are also fundamental to the operation of some network protocols and services such as ... Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.7.2 Ensure Multiple External NTP Servers are set

audit.pattern: (?m)(?s:^set system ntp server \S+.*^set system ntp server \S+.*^set system ntp server \S+)

remediation.command:
! Configure at least 3 External NTP Servers using the following commands under the hierarchy;
set system ntp server <Servers IP>

title: Ensure NTP Boot-Server is set
description: An NTP Boot-Server should be configured for the router to update its time on boot. When the router boots or when a new Routing Engine is installed its time may have drifted or be set beyond the maximum amount where periodic updates can return it to the correct time, resulting in the correct time never being set. To prevent this situation;. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.7.3 Ensure NTP Boot-Server is set

remediation.command:
! To configure an NTP Boot Server, enter the following command from the hierarchy;
set system ntp ntp boot-server <Server IP or Hostname>

title: Ensure NTP uses version 4
description: Version 4 of the NTP protocol should be utilized. NTP is one of the oldest Internet Standard protocols and has been around for over 30 years. As with most protocols, during its lifetime, NTP has received numerous revisions and updates to ensure it remains reliable and secure to use in modern networks. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.7.4 Ensure NTP uses version 4

remediation.command:
! Configure each External NTP Server to use NTP Version 4 using the following commands under the hierarchy:
set system ntp server <Servers IP> version 4

title: Ensure Idle Timeout is Set for Web-Management
description: Idle JWeb sessions should be timed out after 15 minutes. If JWeb Management sessions are left unattended it may be possible for an attacker to use the session to take control of the JUNOS device. To prevent this, or at least limit the scope of such an attack, an idle timeout should be set to end sessions where no ... Passes when web-management is not configured; fails if idle-timeout is missing or above 15 minutes. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.2.4 Ensure Idle Timeout is Set for Web-Management

remediation.command:
! To enable Idle Timeouts for JWeb issue the following command from the hierarchy:
set system services web-management session idle-timeout <Time in Minutes>

title: Ensure Session Limited is Set for Web-Management
description: Concurrent Web-Management sessions should be limited. JUNOS Devices can be managed through a powerful Web Management GUI called JWeb. Operating the JWeb, or any other, management service uses resources on the device's Routing Engine (RE). Passes when web-management is not configured; fails if session-limit is missing or above 5. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.10.2.5 Ensure Session Limited is Set for Web-Management

remediation.command:
! To enable Session limits for JWeb issue the following command from the hierarchy;
set system services web-management session-limit 5

title: Ensure NETCONF Rate Limit is Set
description: If the NETCONF service is configured, the Rate Limit should be set. NETCONF can be configured to use SSH transport to allow remote access while preventing the exposure of sensitive data and authentication details on the network. If configured, the NETCONF-over-SSH service will provide services on port TCP/830. Passes when 'set system services netconf ssh' is not configured; otherwise requires 'set system services netconf ssh rate-limit'. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).

title: Ensure device is physically secured
description: Network Devices should be physically secured. As with most information assets, it is vital that an attacker is prevented from gaining physical access to your Juniper JUNOS Devices. ! While preventing all physical access is nearly impossible in some deployment scenarios, such as for a Service Provider supplying Customer Premises Equipment (CPE), in most cases the following minimum steps should be considered:
- The JUNOS Device should be deployed in a secure, locked room.
- Access logs should be maintained for the room, either electronically through use of access cards or through a manual process for access to the key.
- Access to the room should be limited to only those personnel absolutely required.
- Use of CCTV to monitor sensitive areas and comms rooms.
- The room should ideally be equipped with Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) and cooling facilities as well as be free from Electromagnetic Interference sources. Loss of power (either malicious or accidental) or cooling can result in a loss of service. These methods should be a bare minimum and other physical security options considered when protecting a JUNOS Device which processes or transits sensitive data, such as Encryption Keys, Credit Card or Personally Identifiable Information which may be in scope for regulatory/industry compliance standards such as PCI DSS, GDPR or HIPAA. In these situation Secure Hosting or Co-Location Facilities may be required and options considered for Physical Security should include: - 24/7 Security Guards and Monitoring
- Biometric and/or Multi Factor access control
- Private Caged areas for secure equipment
- Additional alarm and monitoring systems to detect equipment being removed from racks

title: Ensure Retired JUNOS Devices are Disposed of Securely
description: JUNOS Devices must be disposed of securely. As with all systems, there will come a point where a JUNOS Device has reached the end of it's service and must either be redeployed, recycled or disposed of. JUNOS Devices used in production will typically contain a significant store of sensitive information, ... CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Verify that: JUNOS Devices must be disposed of securely

remediation.command:
To ensure that sensitive data is not lost when disposing of or redeploying retired JUNOS Devices, it is essential that the system be fully zeroized. This process returns the system to its original factory default state, with no root password set and all configuration, backups, user specified options, encryption keys, etc deleted. To zeroize a JUNOS Device, log in as a user with the maintenance permission or as root and issue the following command from Operational Mode: root@host>request system zeroize media The media option used above also undertakes a process to securely "scrub" onboard memory and persistent media (such as flash, HDDs or SSDs) using a method equivalent to "clearing" as specified in NIST SP800-88. Using the media option will take significantly more time, as it repeatedly overwrites every area of storage with random data, but is strongly recommended for all devices where the option is supported. An increasing number of JUNOS Devices, such as the PTX5000 Series and some MX Series routers, utilize a Disaggregated JUNOS Operating System which hosts JUNOS as a Virtual Machine abstracting it from the physical Routing Engine hardware. In some instances the request system zeroize command will zeroize the Guest JUNOS VM only, and not the underlying Host OS. For these platforms the following command should be used from Operational Mode: root@host>request vmhost zeroize This command will clear both the JUNOS VM and the Host OS. When some devices, such as EX or QFX Series, are deployed in Clusters, HA or Virtual Chassis environments the request system zeroize media

title: Ensure Hostname is Not Set to Device Make or Model
description: The device make and model should not appear in the hostname. The first step in any attack is reconnaissance. An attacker will attempt to learn about the target network, its hosts and network devices. A key piece of information for an attacker is what type of device he/she is attacking. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.19 Ensure Hostname is Not Set to Device Make or Model

remediation.command:
! To configure the hostname, issue the following command from the hierarchy;
set system host-name <hostname> The hostname should not include any indication of the make or model of the device.

title: Ensure Default Address Selection is Set
description: The primary address configured on the loopback should be used as the source in all JUNOS generated packets. To ensure a consistent source address for traffic from the JUNOS Device, the Loopback address should be configured as the default source address for traffic generated by the Routing Engine. Audited against the output of 'show configuration | display set | no-more' (set format, not the curly-brace hierarchy).
reference: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.20 Ensure Default Address Selection is Set

remediation.command:
! To set the default source address to the loopback interface enter the following command from the hierarchy:
set system default-address-selection Ensure that a loopback address has been configured for the device from the hierarchy.
